statements.statement: There is a contradiction regarding the effectiveness of pure imitation learning for autonomous driving.
One claim states that pure imitation learning is insufficient even with 30 million examples and mid-level input/output representations.
Model failures include getting stuck or colliding with parked vehicles despite viable passing options.
Another claim highlights that this work advances capabilities using purely offline data without reinforcement learning, suggesting progress in imitation learning approaches.
The contradiction centers on whether pure imitation learning alone is sufficient for reliable autonomous driving performance.

parsed.type_evidence: Claims 1 and 3 are cited as being in contradiction: claim 1 says pure imitation learning is not sufficient, claim 3 says the work pushes the boundaries of what can be done with purely offline data and no RL.
